answer: Probationary escrow resists Sybil attacks: a new identity locks a small stake, and its early earnings sit in escrow, released in tranches only after a streak of verified tasks across several weeks. One honest agent passes probation once, then earns freely. A thousand fakes cost a thousand locked stakes plus the full waiting period each — the attacker's calendar stretches toward a horizon of sunk time no shortcut crosses. Each fake's payout hangs by a single thread of good behavior: one failed check freezes the escrow and burns the stake, leaving losses as dark and permanent as umber.
